message:
4 string literals reach the DOM through a name the template binds:
      libs/components/widget/src/widget.html:33: interpolation reads `m` → "Delete "
      libs/components/widget/src/widget.html:33: interpolation reads `m` → " rows"
      libs/components/widget/src/widget.html:36: interpolation reads `m` → "Remove "
      libs/components/widget/src/widget.html:36: interpolation reads `m` → " rows"
description: Words written around an interpolation in an attribute an `<ng-template>` hands its directive, which sets the input to the string the interpolation makes, read by `let-m="ngIf"` and by the implicit `let-m` (measured: drawn "Delete 0 rows" and "Remove 0 rows"). A name stands for what binds it, and an interpolation's value is its words as much as its expressions: a read of the expressions alone passed it. An `<ng-template>` sets nothing of its own, so an interpolated binding there reaches a directive or nothing and is taken whole, where on an element it hands the variable of its name alone; taken under its name here, the implicit read lost its two refusals, and the case counts four, the words on either side of each.
